newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: First Dutch bank reveals hidden reserves.
newsitem.headline: First Dutch bank reveals hidden reserves.

text.p: Nationale Investeringsbank NV (NIB) on Friday became the first Dutch bank to disclose its hidden reserves.
NIB, revealing reserves of 314 million guilders, said however that changes in accounting rules associated with the disclosure would be neutral for its profits in the long term.
Earlier NIB reported that 1996 net profit rose to 156 million guilders from 128 million in 1995.
Dutch banks have been ordered to disclose their hidden reserves for general risks, designated by the Dutch acronym VAR, by the year 2000 to comply with European Union rules.
The hidden reserves will be replaced by a new publicly disclosed reserve, designated by the Dutch acronym FAR.
NIB said it had allocated 300 million guilders to the new FAR reserve and had allocated the remaining 14 million from the VAR to its general reserves.

The old VAR reserve was used to cover loan losses, but from 1997 these will be charged directly to the profit and loss account. The new FAR reserve will be used to cover unpredictable and exceptional losses.
ABN AMRO, the biggest Dutch bank, has indicated that its profits will rise as a result of the changes.
It said this was because future provisions for loan losses will fall, all other things being equal. Analysts said ABN AMRO had overprovided for loan losses in the past.
ABN AMRO is due to disclose its hidden reserves when it publishes its 1996 results next Thursday. ((-- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040))
